Alex / Redwood team,

We started seeing a material regression in our hosted requests starting ~2027-06-08 22:00 UTC. Key symptoms:
- p95 latency up from ~120ms to ~580ms; p99 up to ~1.2s for our chat endpoint.
- Token-per-second throughput per request (our internal measurement) dropped ~45% leading to timeouts on long responses.
- Error rate climbed to ~2.3% (mostly downstream timeouts / 504s) during peak windows.

Attached are a small sample of original requests and the per-request timing snapshots (brightlane_request_samples.jsonl + perf_snaps.log). We rolled no changes on our side. This began roughly when you rolled something last night, per our support rep.

This is impacting checkout conversion on our in-product assistant — can we get immediate help and an ETA for mitigation? Happy to hop on a call.

Thanks,

Quick update from infra side — I pulled the rollout logs for 2027-06-08 21:45 UTC. We did switch a model variant to a new quant profile (q4f16-compat) and enabled a revised kernel selector rule that prefers fused-attention kernels when supported.

Prelim findings:
- Perf snapshots (attached) show that requests with sequence lengths >512 see a disproportionate slowdown. For shorter sequences (<200 tokens) impact is minimal.
- Kernel selection trace for a number of Brightlane requests shows a fallback to the generic GEMM path due to a minor operator shape mismatch introduced by the quant path (we have kernel-diff.patch attached). That fallback forces smaller microbatch sizes and kills throughput.
- Error spikes correlate with queueing during those slower long-request tails.

Attachments: kernel-diff.patch, perf_snaps.log (subset).

Actionable next steps I propose immediately:
- Temp: pin Brightlane's route to the prior quant/model variant (rollback) while we fix the selector logic.
- Short-term config: enable kernel_compat_mode=legacy for their account to force the previous kernel routing.
- Longer-term: add a selector unit-test that includes long-sequence payloads to prevent regressions.

I'll follow up in 15 with a concrete rollback plan.

— Evelyn
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Hosted API - seeing dramatic p95/p99 spikes and token/sec drop since yesterday

Dug into the perf traces and kernel selection logs. Technical summary:
- The new quant profile introduced a slight layout change in the fused attention op for specific model dims. The kernel selector compares op fingerprints and chose the fused-attention kernel when the fingerprint matched; however, for a non-trivial fraction of Brightlane requests the fingerprint now fails (edge shapes with streaming + past-key-values) and selector falls back to a slower, unoptimized matmul path.
- Fallback has two performance hits: (1) no fused attention vectorization, (2) microbatching policy degenerates (we observed per-CPU token loop overhead increasing) which reduces tokens/sec by ~40–55% on our p100/rtx pools.
- The problem is visible primarily on sequences >512 and when streaming is used (because the KV shapes differ).

Proposed immediate mitigation (we can enact in ~20 min):
A) Route Brightlane to the pre-quantized model variant (rollback for their tenant). This is lowest-risk and will restore throughput.
B) If they prefer a config toggle: set account flag kernel_compat_mode=legacy to bypass the new selector for their tenant.
C) Medium-term: fix selector fingerprinting and add a canary that exercises streaming+long-seq codepath.

I've attached a small patch that highlights the kernel selection diff we observed (kernel-diff.patch) and a perf snapshot set (perf_snaps.log).

If Alex/Evelyn confirm, I'll schedule the tenant pin and watch the next 2 peak windows.

— Rishi
Sr. Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

Emily / Marcus — short summary and plan: 
- Root cause (prelim): kernel selector + new quant profile interaction causing fallback to generic matmul path for streaming / long-seq requests. This reduces tokens/sec and increases p95/p99 for affected requests.
- Immediate mitigation (we can do now): pin Brightlane's route to the prior model/quant variant and enable kernel_compat_mode=legacy for the account. Rishi will execute and monitor.
- Expected impact: we expect p95/p99 to return near baseline within the next peak (we'll monitor the next 2 hours closely).
- Next steps: internal postmortem, selector unit-tests for streaming flows, and a safe-rollout gating checklist for quant/kernel changes.

We will proceed with the tenant pin now unless you prefer a different approach. Would you like us to open a brief rolling-change window at 12:30 PM PST so your SREs can observe?

Apologies for the disruption — we understand the conversion impact and will prioritize Brightlane until fully stabilized. I'll keep you updated every 30 minutes during the mitigation.
